findings.title: Unscoped display picker bypasses Owner/Manager People-directory boundary
findings.status: confirmed by independent synthetic actual-route probe; awaiting Architect second reader
findings.acceptance: docs/FEATURE_SPEC.md:136; shared mandatory criteria: mounted operations enforce current role/target authority and privacy
findings.reproduction: In disposable loopback PostgreSQL, create Owner, Member, Viewer and another Member in one project; create no boards/grants. With Member or Viewer session, GET /api/v1/projects/prj/members returns403. GET /api/v1/projects/prj/people and ?purpose=display return200 and all active project user IDs/display names/avatars/roles. GET ?purpose=mention correctly returns empty data.
findings.impact: Any active Member/Viewer can enumerate project identities despite being denied the full directory; no board eligibility is required. Email addresses are not exposed by this path, but the user decision prohibits directory data and allows only scoped assignee/mention pickers for these roles.
findings.counterevidence: /members uses correct Owner/Manager enforcement and existing People policy tests pass10/10 with runtime checks; scoped mention/assignee checks are not sufficient because purpose defaults to display. API.md74 still documents the older behavior; FEATURE_SPEC latest explicit user decision supersedes it.
findings.suggestedFix: Gate display/default directory access to current Owner/Manager using the same transaction/lock authority as /members, or retire display if no accepted consumer needs it. Preserve board-scoped assignee/mention behavior. Add explicit omitted/display/boardId+display negative tests for Member/Viewer and role demotion races.
